title: Finite-size spin chain sensitivity
question: Do finite-size entanglement diagnostics remain consistent across an expanded set of synthetic Hamiltonian controls?

scope.in_scope: Offline finite spin-chain numerical models and frozen public synthetic benchmarks.
scope.out_of_scope: Measured quantum hardware, claims of a new physical law, or revisions to frozen QP5 results.

evidence.source_description: Existing ΦField Lab finite-chain outputs with known simulator assumptions and declared model limitations.
evidence.replay_plan: Recompute with independent code paths and preserve exact solver parameters.

evaluation.method: Propose matched finite-size sweeps and negative controls before any numerical execution.
evaluation.metric: Deviation between model predictions and independent finite-chain baselines
evaluation.baseline: Previously frozen finite-size benchmark results on matched inputs.
evaluation.negative_control: Apply geometry-preserving null parameter changes and compare noise floors.
evaluation.success_criterion: Computed trends reproduce on held-out finite sizes within predefined tolerances.
evaluation.failure_criterion: Any retained candidate depends on leakage, unmatched controls, or solver numerical instability.
evaluation.uncertainty: Finite-size effects, boundary sensitivity, and eigensolver precision must be reported.

candidates.hypothesis: A proposed finite-size entanglement trend persists across the declared held-out sizes.
candidates.prediction: Matched models recover the predeclared qualitative relationship.
candidates.falsifier: Any held-out matched numerical case violates the declared relationship.

candidates.hypothesis: The apparent trend is entirely caused by one chosen boundary condition.
candidates.prediction: Changing the boundary condition eliminates the reported trend.
candidates.falsifier: The relationship persists under appropriately matched alternative boundaries.

risk.potential_harms: Synthetic model results can be mistaken for independent experimental physics.
risk.stop_condition: Stop if model provenance is absent or the protocol is not frozen before testing.
